title: Round-Robin Warp Scheduler
constraints: 4 warps. A warp is **eligible** at an edge if `ready[w] = 1` and it did not issue at either of the two previous edges (a 2-cycle pipeline hazard window).

Among the eligible warps, pick the first one starting at a round-robin pointer (circular). The pointer then moves to the warp after the winner. With no eligible warp, nothing issues and the pointer stays.
Outputs are registered: `issue_valid` / `issue_warp` describe the decision made at the last edge (`issue_warp` is don't-care when `issue_valid = 0`).
Synchronous reset: pointer 0, no blocked warps, no issue. Must be synthesizable.
hints: Keep a small countdown per warp: load 2 when it issues, decrement otherwise. A warp is eligible only when its counter was 0 before the edge.
Selection is the same rotate / priority-encode / rotate-back structure as a round-robin arbiter.
With all warps ready, the issue sequence is 0, 1, 2, 3, 0, … Each warp waits 3 cycles, which covers its window.

examples.title: single warp
examples.expected: issues at most every third cycle: 2, -, -, 2, -, -
